chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: New York musicians wait to replace the band at rehearsal
summary: At the Apollo rehearsal local players waited for mistakes, but the sharp 14-piece Chicago band sent them away; Quinn Wilson told the same story of Hines.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you used to -- your Chicago band used to --

Yeah, I used the band from Chicago, and I can tell you a funny story. When we went to New York, Thursday, you open on a Friday, and so Thursday afternoon, evening, you had the rehearsal. All of the guys from the -- the local guys would come in with their horns. And they would just sit there waiting for you to goof up so they could get hired.
And after about an hour of rehearsal, they would even bend over the guys and turn the music for them. These guys were really something.

In the '50s, right. And so, they -- after about an hour, -- we had such a good band at that time, and it was a good reading band, sharp on shows and everything. After about an hour, the hall thinned out and there was nobody there but us.
How many were in the band then?
14. It's interesting, you told me that story, because Quinn told me the very same story. It happened in the Earl Hines --
Oh, yeah, New York -- I'm telling you -- and the hall was packed. It was full of musicians. But after they found out that nothing was coming out, they all disappeared.
There used to be an after-hours --
